answers.assumption_check: Assumed and measured at n=2 hosts idle (53 s, 24 s) plus one load exceedance (>120 s, the live trouble): that sweep load, not a hang, explains the timeout. Unmeasured: the proof's wall under the sweep itself; 300 s is a margin, to be re-measured at the next sweep. 2026-11-19, the proof is slow only under load: Windows idle 53 s wall (12 of 12 green, bin/cairn test); Linux idle 23.4 s and 24.2 s (akienasus_cc_0, origin/main 3c6c6c3a1, unsealed, 12 of 12 PASS, no hang); under cc_0's 39-validation reseal sweep on the Dell (22:44-23:05) it exceeded the default 120 s and went red (seal-red-...-test-seal-is-never-silently-dropped). Its own waits are bounded (subprocess timeout=240, bus ask timeout=180), no sleep loop.
